SEC-HD-V8-01.note: Head 'shipment' singular; 'since the war' forces present perfect. Header states both facts, so D is the only cell of the number x aspect grid that fits without reading. The tense trigger does sit downstream of the blank, but ~8 words out, not 4.

SEC-HD-V8-02.note: Supplement opened with a comma must close with a comma, killing B/D. Header does not say the head is singular, so a glance at 'The east range' is still needed to choose A over C.

SEC-HD-V8-03.note: 'who' is subject of 'had falsified' across the interpolated 'the others believed'; identifying clause takes no commas. Header names subjective case AND restrictive, which uniquely selects B.

SEC-HD-V8-04.note: Participle must attach to a person, and the past frame is closed. Header gives both, leaving only B.

SEC-HD-V8-05.note: 'not only the number of stoppages' is a noun phrase, so the second member must be one. B fails 'but also'; C/D restate the verb. Needed the stem to know the first member's category, hence helpful not decisive.

SEC-HD-V8-06.note: 'more than one' takes a singular verb; closed season blocks present perfect. Header hands over both halves; B is the only singular simple past.

SEC-HD-V8-07.note: Two surveyors, plural possessive; 'that' clause restrictive so no comma. Header states apostrophe-after-plural and no-comma-before-that, which is the answer.

SEC-HD-V8-08.note: Linking 'smells' takes predicate adjective 'sweet'; head 'A cellar' singular. Header asserts both, selecting C outright.

SEC-HD-V8-09.note: 'each of' singular plus 'already' at a stated past moment. C is the only past perfect on offer, so the header alone picks it.

SEC-HD-V8-10.note: Gerund subject 'reconciling...' is singular; 'In the years the wharf was in use' closes the frame. Header names both; D is the singular simple past.

SEC-HD-V8-11.note: 'as well as' does not compound the subject; completed event takes simple past. C uniquely.

SEC-HD-V8-12.note: 'The tracings' plural across 'along with'; passive required. The two progressive-active options are eliminable without the passage ('the tracings were losing' is impossible), so at least one distractor is dead weight.

SEC-HD-V8-13.note: Third member of a to-infinitive series. Header says finite clause is out and members must be one kind, which leaves only the infinitive.

SEC-HD-V8-14.note: Antecedent is 'The two presses' (with the font), not the nearest singular noun, so 'their'; finished past so 'was' with singular 'type'. The mixed number inside one option ('their ... type was') is the genuinely hard part, and the header pre-resolves it.

SEC-HD-V8-15.note: Interrupter 'in the same wallet as the awards themselves' closes with a comma; 'a list' must not be cut from 'of every hedge'. The very next word after the blank is 'of', which alone kills C and D.

SEC-HD-V8-16.note: Supplement opened at 'a volume rebound...' must close with a comma, and no colon may separate 'records' from its object list. Header states exactly those two, giving B.

SEC-HD-V8-17.note: Semicolon plus 'consequently,'. B ('convenience. Consequently') is defensible as clause boundary under any convention; it fails only on the comma after the conjunctive adverb, which some house styles omit. Header's second clause ('adverb ... is followed by a comma') is what forces D over B, and without it I would have hesitated.

SEC-HD-V8-18.note: Proximity agreement with 'the village schoolmaster'; closed decade blocks present perfect. Singular simple past = D.

SEC-HD-V8-19.note: 'The remains' is plural-only across a long singular modifier; the state is current. A.

SEC-HD-V8-20.note: 'The clauses' plural; the span closed. B is the plural simple past.

SEC-HD-V8-21.note: Counterfactual antecedent takes past perfect; 'would have' belongs to the consequent, which is already present after the blank. Header says past perfect and D is the only one.

SEC-HD-V8-22.note: Comma closes 'Because the stores had to be got at in a hurry'; 'the lockers the yard had fitted' is identifying, so no internal commas. C.

SEC-HD-V8-23.note: Backshift after 'reported' gives 'would', and the seam is acted on, so passive. C. The two 'will' options are eliminable on backshift alone.

SEC-HD-V8-24.note: 'one of the very few works ... that credit' agrees with 'works'; restrictive, no comma. Header names both and picks A.

cross_item_heuristic.summary: Substantially. The batch is built to one rigid template and the template is visible from the option sets alone.

heuristics.name: 2x2 grid collapse
heuristics.description: On every form/agreement item the four options are the cross product of {singular, plural} x {simple past/present, present perfect}. So there is exactly one number question and one aspect question, and each is binary. Any partial knowledge halves the field twice.

heuristics.name: beat the attractor
heuristics.description: The head noun is always separated from the blank by a modifier ending in a plural noun (blades, tenants, pits, the two of them, ensembles, pattern books, schoolmaster-after-adjusters). Pick the number that DISAGREES with the noun nearest the blank. Held on every item I applied it to.
heuristics.exceptions: 12, 19, 20 invert it (plural head, singular-ish tail), so it is direction-sensitive, not blind.

heuristics.name: present perfect is almost always the trap
heuristics.description: A dated or closed time frame is named in 8 of the 9 tense items, so 'have/has been X' is a distractor. It is the key exactly once (item 01, the only 'since ...' span). Guessing 'never the perfect' scores 8/9.

heuristics.name: balanced punctuation wins
heuristics.description: On every boundaries item the key is the option whose marks are symmetric or absent: comma-in/comma-out for a supplement, and NO mark where a restrictive clause or a noun+PP is broken. The option with one lone comma, or a dash answering a comma, is never the key.

heuristics.name: letter balance
heuristics.description: My 24 picks come out exactly 6 A / 6 B / 6 C / 6 D. That is a deliberate spread rather than a leak per item, but a solver who had 18 confident answers could force several of the remaining six from the count - the same mechanism as the ABCD-permutation tell already on record.

cross_item_heuristic.residual_difficulty_without_headers: With headers stripped the batch would still be solvable well above chance by the two rules above, but items 03, 14, 15 and 17 would be genuinely contested.

header_summary.verdict: The headers function as an answer key, not as a signpost. Each one does not merely name the skill - it states the RESOLUTION of every binary the item turns on: 'a singular head', 'the present perfect required', 'restrictive', 'takes the subjective case', 'the past perfect', 'agrees with the nearer subject'. Because the four options are always the cross product of exactly those binaries, asserting both values names one cell. On 22 of 24 items I could have produced my pick from the header text and the option list with the passage covered entirely. The two exceptions are 02 (header says the verb answers to the head noun but does not say the head is singular) and 05 (header says the second member matches the first in kind but does not say the first is a noun phrase) - in both, one short look at the stem finished it.
header_summary.recommendation: If these headers ship to students, or are shown to graders during a blind attack, the measurement is contaminated: a blind margin computed with headers present measures header quality, not item quality. Rewrite them to name the skill and the rule family only ('subject-verb agreement across an intervening clause; verb aspect'), never the resolved value ('singular', 'present perfect', 'restrictive'). Item 14 is the clearest case - the whole difficulty is deciding whether the determiner looks back to the presses or to the font, and the header decides it in advance.
